key_insight: LLMs are moving front-end EDA from narrow assistance toward agentic systems that can generate HDL, build testbenches, and support design-space exploration from shared specifications.
engineering_relevance: For chip design teams, this suggests a path to faster specification-to-implementation workflows, improved productivity in high-level synthesis, and more integrated automation of early design tasks.
method: Review evolution of EDA from localized assistance to autonomous agentic execution
Survey LLM use cases in front-end design: specification understanding, HDL generation, testbench construction, and design-space exploration
Discuss opportunities and challenges for deploying agentic AI systems such as OpenClaw in EDA
evidence_signal: The paper is a perspective/review rather than an experimental study, so its evidence is based on synthesizing representative advances and workflows discussed in the literature.
watch_item: LLM-driven EDA remains limited by reliability, correctness verification, and integration into safety-critical hardware design flows.
paper_title: LLM for EDA in Front-End Design: Challenges and Opportunities
